Post Lab

The festival look on the Lantern Festival street: seven full-screen effects after the frame is drawn. Change how they run and watch the post timeline against its 4 ms budget, split into bandwidth and math.

Festival street, mid-range phone. Goal: post ≤ 4 ms and GPU ≤ 28 ms, both walking and in the rod zoom, with bloom and the zoom blur kept.

Lesson 031: post-processing budgets

    
    
    
    Lesson 034 · Challenge · predict first, then tap Set up
    
    
      
  
      

  
      
    
      What this shows
      
    
      
      
      Touching the screen costs
      Reading and writing 1,152,000 pixels of HDR colour moves about 18.4 MB: about 0.9 ms before any math. Three tiny effects as three passes cost 3.1 ms.
      
      
      Run it only where it shows
      Depth of field while walking blurred nothing and cost 7 ms. Blurry effects don't need full resolution: bloom at half resolution keeps the glow for 1.6 ms instead of 5.2.
      
      
      Bytes are the phone's limit
      Half the bytes per pixel halves the bandwidth part of every pass, not the math. After the fixes, post is 2.7 ms walking and 3.45 ms zoomed.
      
    
      
    
      This lab is a simulation, not a measurement. It uses the lesson's numbers: scene 15.81 ms, a bandwidth floor of about 0.9 ms per full-screen 64-bit pass, the per-pass split of bandwidth and math from the lesson, and 32-bit HDR halving every pass's bandwidth. Real costs depend on the GPU, the driver and how passes are scheduled; real anti-aliasing usually runs on 8-bit colour after tonemapping. The picture is an illustration.
